title: Mosaic books presuppose immortality and prove resurrection — Christ vs the Sadducees
source_text: XXVI. Sed aliquid gravius est quo putant adversarii se posse probare Scripturam, quamdiu saltem solis libris Mosaicis constitit, omnia ad salutem necessaria non continuisse. Nec enim quicquam ad fidem & salutem magis necessarium fingi potest, quam dogma de animorum immortalitate & resurrectione corporum. At, inquiunt, de dogmatibus istis tanti momenti apud Mosen nihil reperitur. Quod ad primum attinet, animorum nempe immortalitatem, dico rem esse quam omnis religio praesupponit. Etenim si a brutis eatenus non differimus, animaeque nostrae non secus ac pecudum, cum corporibus intereunt, nec quicquam hominis post mortem superest, frustra est pietas, & frustra religio: nec aliud restat, quam ut cum profanis dicamus, Edamus, bibamus, cras enim moriemur. Itaque, quandoquidem libri Mosis toti occupantur in tradenda religione & cultu Dei praescribendo, animae immortalitas a Mose praesupponitur, estque aliquid quod ex generali librorum ejus scopo doctrinaque in eis contenta indubitate & aperte deducitur. Sed praeterea sunt multa singularia loca apud Mosen unde non tantummodo animae immortalitas, sed corporum resurrectio probari & colligi potest. Nam utrumque Christus contra Sadducaeos confirmat ex illis Dei verbis, Ego sum Deus Abrahami, Deus Isaac, & Deus Jacobi, quoniam, ut inquit, Deus non est Deus mortuorum, sed Deus viventium. Atque adeo Christus Sadducaeos erroris hac in parte arguens ad Scripturam eos revocat, & illis ignorantiam Scripturarum exprobrat. Erratis, inquit, nescientes Scripturas. Unde manifestum est, doctrinam istam illis ex Scriptura notam esse debuisse. Adde quod, si ponamus doctrinam de resurrectione obscure tantum fuisse Mosaicis libris insinuatam, probari non poterit claram & distinctam ejus fidem etiam tunc fuisse ad salutem necessariam.
pass_a_gloss: But there is something graver by which the adversaries think they can prove that Scripture, at least while it consisted of the Mosaic books alone, did not contain all things necessary to salvation. For nothing more necessary to faith and salvation can be imagined than the dogma of the immortality of souls and the resurrection of bodies. But, they say, nothing is found in Moses concerning those dogmas of such moment. As to the first, namely the immortality of souls, I say it is a matter which every religion presupposes. For if we do not differ from beasts so far, and our souls like cattle's perish with the bodies, and nothing of man remains after death, piety is vain, and religion vain: and nothing remains but that we say with the profane, Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. Therefore, since Moses' books are wholly occupied in handing down religion and prescribing the worship of God, the immortality of the soul is presupposed by Moses, and is something which is indubitably and openly deduced from the general scope of his books and the doctrine contained in them. But besides there are many particular places in Moses from which not only the immortality of the soul but the resurrection of bodies can be proved and gathered. For Christ confirms both against the Sadducees from those words of God, I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, because, as He says, God is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living. And so Christ, convicting the Sadducees of error in this point, recalls them to Scripture, and reproaches them with ignorance of the Scriptures. You err, He says, not knowing the Scriptures. Whence it is plain that that doctrine ought to have been known to them from Scripture. Add that if we suppose the doctrine of the resurrection was only obscurely hinted in the Mosaic books, it cannot be proved that a clear and distinct faith of it was even then necessary to salvation.
pass_b_english: Graver still: they say Moses alone never contained all needful to salvation — immortality and resurrection are missing.
Immortality every religion presupposes: if souls die like cattle, piety is vain — eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Moses' whole scope is religion and worship; soul-immortality is presupposed and openly drawn from that scope.
Particular Mosaic texts also prove resurrection: Christ vs the Sadducees cites I am the God of Abraham... — God of the living, not the dead.
He blames their ignorance of the Scriptures; if resurrection was only obscure then, clear distinct faith of it was not yet required for salvation.
